subject.title: docs cat drops person smart chips from all output modes (plain, --plain, --json); readable only via --raw

question: Should `docs cat` keep legacy text unchanged by default with opt-in chip rendering, or render smart chips by default and provide a compatibility mode?
rationale: The omission is a source-proven bug, but repository policy prioritizes stable scriptable output, so automation cannot choose the permanent default-output contract.

options.title: Opt-in text, additive JSON
options.body: Keep legacy text by default, add `--chips`, and expose typed chips plus rendered text as additive JSON fields.

options.title: Render by default
options.body: Include chips in normal text output and add an explicit compatibility mode for existing scripts.

options.title: Structured JSON only
options.body: Expose typed chip metadata for automation but leave all readable text output unchanged.

recommendation.title: Opt-in text, additive JSON
recommendation.body: Keep legacy text by default, add `--chips`, and expose typed chips plus rendered text as additive JSON fields.

likelyOwner.reason: The original command, current extraction implementation, and most read-path history trace to this owner.
